name: Light Magenta
lede: Light Magenta is a bright, pale-leaning pink-violet, a name made by adding light to magenta, which was itself named for a dye of 1859.

sections.title: A modifier name
sections.body: Light Magenta is a plain descriptive name, built from light plus magenta, and our library traces the swatch to the 2010 xkcd color survey [1]. The ISCC-NBS system calls the nearest block brilliant purple, 11.5 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale, so the fit to any standard name is loose [1].

sections.title: The dye behind the word
sections.body:
The word magenta comes from a dye. Eckstut credits the French chemist Verguin with the first magenta dye in 1859 [2], and Greenfield adds that French chemists created fuchsine that year, which some called solferino or magenta after a bloody battle in Italy [3]. Like [[mauve]], it was worn by Empress Eugénie and became very popular [3].

In color science, magenta ink works by soaking up green light, so what the paper sends back is the red and blue [2]. Livingstone notes that cyan, magenta and yellow are the most efficient printing primaries [4]. So a light magenta on screen is made by lighting red and blue together, which is a different recipe from the ink [2][4]. The base color has its own article at [[magenta]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering even 1 per cent of its canvas, as photographed [5]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole [5].
